papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.abstract: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory to ground generation.

papers.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique
papers.abstract: Self-reflection reduces unsupported claims in retrieval-augmented models.

verified_claims.text: RAG grounds generation in retrieved passages, reducing unsupported statements.
Self-critique mechanisms improve citation fidelity in QA settings.

research_gaps.description: Few standardized benchmarks quantify hallucination rates in biomedical QA with RAG.

report.title: RAG Hallucination Mitigation in Scientific QA
report.executive_summary: Retrieval-augmented generation reduces unsupported generations by grounding answers in cited evidence spans. Biomedical QA still lacks standardized hallucination benchmarks.

key_findings.text: RAG combines retrieval with generation to anchor responses in source documents.
Self-critique in retrieval pipelines improves citation fidelity.

research_gaps.text: Biomedical RAG hallucination benchmarks remain underdeveloped.

future_opportunities.text: Develop biomedical QA hallucination evaluation suites with claim-level grounding.

recommendations.text: Enforce claim verification gates before executive brief synthesis.

report.limitations: Benchmark fast-path uses curated hero corpus for demo latency targets.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Collaboration via LangGraph for Research Workflows
papers.abstract: Decomposed agents improve verification and orchestration for literature synthesis.

papers.title: Stateful Agent Graphs for Auditable Scientific Reasoning
papers.abstract: Checkpointed graphs preserve provenance across discovery, verification, and synthesis.

verified_claims.text: Specialized agents outperform monolithic prompts on verification-heavy research tasks.
Stateful orchestration enables reproducible multi-step research sessions.

research_gaps.description: Limited benchmarks quantify OpenTelemetry coverage across LangGraph research pipelines.

report.title: Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration for Research
report.executive_summary: Decomposed discovery, verification, and synthesis agents improve grounding and auditability compared with single-shot RAG.

key_findings.text: Verification-specialized agents improve claim grounding quality.
Graph-based orchestration preserves provenance across pipeline stages.

research_gaps.text: Observability standards for multi-agent research graphs remain immature.

future_opportunities.text: Standardize per-agent OpenTelemetry spans in research pipelines.

recommendations.text: Deploy checkpointed LangGraph pipelines for reproducible research intelligence.
